QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_34

question.text: In the context of ETIRD, what does a calendar spread involve?

answer.text: Simultaneous purchase and sale of the same contract type but with different expiry months
Buying a call and selling a put at the same strike and expiry
Taking positions in two different types of bonds
Buying options and selling futures on the same underlying

explanation.text: The Logic: A calendar spread takes opposite positions in the same contract across different expiry months (workbook pp. 190 and 192); the same logic also applies as a time spread in options (workbook p. 173). For example, long June futures and short September futures on the same underlying. The Trap: A call-put combination at the same strike and expiry is a synthetic position, not a calendar spread. Positions in two different bonds form an inter-bond spread (workbook p. 190), not a calendar spread. Mixing options and futures is a different strategy entirely. Note: Calendar spreads keep the same underlying and same contract type but change the expiry month; this is the defining feature in the workbook.
